sections.subtitle: Contact us
sections.content: Conor Moore, Global Head, KPMG Private Enterprise, KPMG International & Partner, KPMG in the US. Lindsay Hull, Senior Director, Emerging Giants Global Network, KPMG Private Enterprise, KPMG International.

You know KPMG. You might not know KPMG Private Enterprise. KPMG Private Enterprise advisers in KPMG firms around the world are dedicated to working with you and your business, no matter where you are in your growth journey - whether you're looking to reach new heights, embrace technology, plan for an exit, or manage the transition of wealth or your business to the next generation. You gain access to KPMG firms' global resources through a single point of contact a professional adviser to your company. It is a local touch with a global reach.

KPMG Private Enterprise's global network for emerging giants has extensive knowledge and experience working with the startup ecosystem. Whether you are looking to establish your operations, raise capital, expand abroad, or simply comply with regulatory requirements we can help. From seed to speed, we're here throughout your journey.

KPMG uses PitchBook as the provider of venture data for the Venture Pulse report. Please note that the M&A and IPO data is not intended to be comprehensive as the report only focuses on venture-backed exits. PitchBook's exit criteria does not include going public via SPAC.

sections.subtitle: PitchBook's deal definitions:
sections.content: Venture capital deals: PitchBook includes equity investments into startup companies from an outside source. Investment does not necessarily have to be taken from an institutional investor. This can include investment from individual angel investors, angel groups, seed funds, venture capital firms, corporate venture firms and corporate investors. Investments received as part of an accelerator program are not included, however, if the accelerator continues to invest in follow-on rounds, those further financings are included. All financings are of companies headquartered in the US. The impact of initial coin offerings on early-stage venture financing as of yet remains indeterminate. Initial coin offerings (ICOs) are excluded from this report's base of data.

sections.subtitle: Venture capital deal stages:
sections.content:
PitchBook assigns deals to stages based on the series of the financing, the company's previous rounds, and the company's founding date. The stages are categorized as follows:
- Pre-seed/Seed: Financings categorized as Pre-seed or Seed, or if the company has not received prior venture capital and is less than two years old.
- Early-stage VC: Financings categorized as Series A or Series B.
- Late-stage VC: Financings categorized as Series C or later.
- Venture growth: Financings categorized as Venture growth, or if a company has been venture-backed, has not raised a round in the last two years, and is at least five years old.

sections.subtitle: Exits:
sections.content: PitchBook includes the first majority liquidity event for investors of a company (since 1990). This includes events where there is a public listing, secondary buyout, or acquisition. The data also includes partial exits where the company was acquired but remained independent. Please note that the M&A and IPO data is not intended to be comprehensive as the report only focuses on venture-backed exits. PitchBook's exit criteria does not include going public via SPAC.

sections.subtitle: Fundraising:
sections.content: PitchBook defines venture capital funds as pools of capital raised for the purpose of investing in the equity of startup companies. In addition to funds raised by traditional venture capital firms, PitchBook also includes funds raised by any institution with the primary intent stated above. Funds identified as growth-stage vehicles are classified as PE funds and are not included in this report. A fund's location is determined by the country in which the fund is domiciled, if that information is not available, it is tied to the principal office of the investing firm. Fundraising data is based on the year the fund held its final close.
